hot_topics.synthesis: Apple has significantly raised subscription prices for Apple TV and Apple One services, marking the fourth increase in four years. Monthly and annual costs for Apple TV+ have climbed by up to 20 percent, now reaching $14.99 per month or $119 annually. This move continues a trend of rising prices for Apple's streaming and bundled offerings.

American communities are increasingly terminating contracts with Flock Safety over concerns about unchecked surveillance, data sharing, high costs, and police misuse of their camera systems. A new survey indicates that more Americans now oppose police license plate cameras than support them, reflecting growing public unease. In August 2026 alone, 90 localities ended their relationships with Flock.

hot_topics.topic: Anthropic's Legal Victory Against Trump Administration Blacklisting
hot_topics.synthesis: AI startup Anthropic has achieved a legal victory against the Trump administration, with a federal judge ruling that the company was illegally blacklisted as a supply-chain risk. This decision comes amidst Anthropic's ongoing disputes with the Pentagon regarding the military's use of AI. The ruling indicates that the previous administration unlawfully retaliated against the AI firm.

hot_topics.topic: Devastating Floods in Nepal and Tibet
hot_topics.synthesis: Deadly flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have caused widespread devastation, with satellite images revealing entire villages, bridges, and a key border crossing washed away. Hundreds of families are anxiously awaiting news of missing loved ones, and rescuers fear a new barrier lake formed by a recent landslide could trigger further flooding. Chinese authorities are reportedly withholding dramatic footage and information about victims in Tibet.

items.title: Apple One and Apple TV subscription prices increase by up to 20 percent
items.summary: Apple has increased the monthly and annual subscription prices for Apple TV by up to 20 percent, marking the fourth such hike in four years. The Apple TV monthly price is now $15, and the annual price is $119.

items.title: Cities terminate Flock contracts at record pace in August
items.summary: American localities are increasingly terminating contracts with Flock Safety for surveillance cameras, with 90 cities doing so in August 2026 due to concerns over surveillance, data sharing, high costs, and police tool abuse.

items.title: Meta makes AI glasses slightly less creepy with limit on nonconsensual recording
items.summary: Meta is implementing a fix for its AI glasses to prevent non-consensual recordings by ensuring the camera stops working if the recording indicator light is covered. This update addresses backlash over users circumventing the privacy safeguard.

items.title: Our 10 favorite scenes from T2: Judgment Day
items.summary: James Cameron's "Terminator 2: Judgment Day" is celebrating its 35th anniversary with a special theatrical rerelease, prompting a look back at favorite scenes from the seminal sci-fi action blockbuster. The film's unexpected success in 1984 led to its highly anticipated sequel.

items.title: Your Book Review: Thomas Urquhart’s Translation Of Rabelais
items.summary: This book review examines Thomas Urquhart's celebrated translation of Rabelais through the lens of Urquhart's own life, portraying him as an aristocrat deeply immersed in studies and duels, yet comically inept as a soldier amidst 17th-century Scottish conflicts.

items.title: 'Not far enough' - US parents and teens on Meta's new limits for young users
items.summary: US parents and teenagers believe Meta's newly announced restrictions for young users, part of an $18 billion child-safety lawsuit settlement, are insufficient.

items.title: 97-year-old woman rescued after Nepali floods looked like 'a warrior'
items.summary: A 97-year-old woman, Guna Maya Bohara, miraculously survived and was rescued using an excavator after the recent flash floods in Nepal.

items.title: BBC tracks one week of Israeli settler violence in occupied West Bank
items.summary: The BBC has documented a week of Israeli settler attacks against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

items.title: Berlin is being blackmailed by hackers, mayor says
items.summary: Berlin's mayor, Kai Wegner, announced that the German capital is being blackmailed by hackers for stolen data but will not succumb to their ransom demand.

items.title: Dutch court sentences man to life over Rwanda genocide
items.summary: A Dutch court in The Hague has sentenced a 66-year-old man to life imprisonment after convicting him of war crimes and genocide related to the Rwandan genocide.

items.title: Footage of Tibet floods isn't being shown in China - and we know little about victims there
items.summary: Dramatic footage from the deadly flash flooding in Tibet is reportedly being hidden from public view in China, leaving little known about the victims.

items.title: Greenland says findings on genocide allegation not final
items.summary: Greenland has stated that the findings regarding allegations of genocide, specifically the use of forced contraception on the Inuit community during the 1960s and 70s, are not yet final.

items.title: King Haakon begins reign after turbulent year for Norwegian monarchy
items.summary: King Haakon has commenced his reign, inheriting a turbulent period for the Norwegian monarchy.

items.title: Norway mourns King Harald as Haakon VIII ascends throne
items.summary: Norway is mourning the death of King Harald, as his son, Haakon VIII, ascends to the throne, adopting the family motto "all for norway."

items.title: Norway's King Harald dies aged 89: A beloved monarch buffeted by family crises
items.summary: Norway's King Harald has died at the age of 89 after a 35-year reign, remembered as a beloved monarch who broke tradition by marrying a commoner.

items.title: Oslo mayor calls off wedding ceremony after death of Norway's king
items.summary: Anne Lindboe, the mayor of Oslo, has canceled her wedding ceremony following the death of Norway's King Harald.

items.title: Right-wing commentator Milo Yiannopoulos detained by ICE
items.summary: British citizen and right-wing commentator Milo Yiannopoulos, who resides in the US and has supported Trump and ICE, has been detained by ICE.

items.title: Russia ramps up rhetoric but wants to avoid war with Nato, Western officials say
items.summary: Western officials state that Russia is escalating its rhetoric but aims to avoid direct war with NATO, although Moscow is expected to continue "hybrid activity" against member states.

items.title: Satellite images reveal scale of flood devastation in Nepal villages
items.summary: Satellite images vividly show the extensive devastation caused by floodwaters in Nepal, revealing villages, bridges, and a critical Nepal-Tibet border crossing washed away.

items.title: Shootings surge as drug gangs torment Brussels
items.summary: Brussels is experiencing a surge in shootings, with over 65 recorded this year, as drug gangs continue to cause torment in the Belgian capital.

items.title: Tate brothers blast US jail conditions as they seek bail in UK extradition fight
items.summary: Andrew and Tristan Tate are criticizing US jail conditions while seeking bail in a Miami court as part of their UK extradition battle, arguing they are not a flight risk.

items.title: Thieves steal 600-diamond necklace from Vienna museum in broad daylight
items.summary: Police are searching for two suspects who stole a 600-diamond necklace from a Vienna museum during daylight hours, believed to have bought tickets to access the exhibition.

items.title: This Indian pilgrim was about to enter Tibet for her dream tour - then her WhatsApp messages stopped
items.summary: An Indian pilgrim's family is anxiously awaiting news after her WhatsApp messages ceased during a trip to the Nepal-Tibet border, where deadly flash floods occurred.

items.title: Trump administration illegally retaliated against Anthropic, judge rules
items.summary: A judge has ruled that the Trump administration unlawfully retaliated against the AI startup Anthropic, which had been in dispute with the Pentagon over military AI use.

items.title: Two-year curfew lifted in Sudan's capital
items.summary: A two-year curfew has been lifted in Sudan's capital, 18 months after military authorities retook control of the city, though conflict persists in other regions.

items.title: US plans to cut off military aid to key Middle East ally, BBC told
items.summary: Iraqi Kurdistan expresses fears of increased vulnerability to Iranian attacks as the US, under the Trump administration, reportedly plans to cut off military aid to the key Middle East ally.

items.title: Violence breaks out in Ceuta as migrant crisis continues
items.summary: Violence has erupted in Ceuta amidst an ongoing migrant crisis, involving a group of migrants throwing stones at a military vehicle and some locals setting migrant camps on fire.

items.title: Watch: Stargazers around the world glimpse 'Blood Moon' lunar eclipse
items.summary: Stargazers worldwide had the opportunity to witness a rare 'Blood Moon' lunar eclipse, an event where the Sun, Earth, and Moon align in the night sky.

items.title: Watch: Why rescuers fear new barrier lake could cause another Nepal-Tibet flood
items.summary: Rescuers are concerned that a new barrier lake formed by a recent landslide near the Nepal-Tibet border could trigger another devastating flood.

items.title: World's youngest reigning traditional monarch dies aged 34
items.summary: King Oyo, who ascended the throne of Uganda's Tooro kingdom at age three, has died at 34, marking the end of the world's youngest reigning traditional monarch's rule.

items.title: Get your Windows license refund
items.summary: This resource provides information on how users can seek a refund for their Windows license.

items.title: GLM-5.3 is now open-weight
items.summary: The GLM-5.3 model has been released as open-weight, making its parameters publicly accessible.

items.title: GUIs should be fully keyboard-driven
items.summary: The opinion piece argues that graphical user interfaces (GUIs) should be designed to be entirely operable via keyboard.

items.summary: This 2018 article explains a remarkably fast method for computing volume using the divergence theorem.

items.title: Htmx 4.0

items.title: Inception-style curved map for turn-by-turn directions
items.summary: A new demo showcases an "Inception-style" curved map interface designed for turn-by-turn navigation directions.

items.summary: A federal judge has ruled that the Trump administration acted illegally by blacklisting the AI company Anthropic.

items.title: Just the rumour of a bug is enough to find an exploit these days
items.summary: This article discusses how even a rumor of a bug can be sufficient to lead to the discovery of a security exploit.

items.title: Luanti removed from Google Play due to baseless AI copyright notice
items.summary: The Luanti app was removed from Google Play after receiving a copyright notice related to AI, which the developers claim is baseless.

items.title: Migrating to HTTPX2
items.summary: This document from OpenAI provides guidance on migrating to the HTTPX2 version of their Python library.

items.title: The Twelve-Factor App (2025)
items.summary: This resource outlines the principles of the Twelve-Factor App methodology for building robust and scalable software-as-a-service applications.

items.title: U.S. sanctions against the A/I Collective
items.summary: The U.S. has imposed sanctions against the A/I Collective, an Italian hosting provider, following its designation as a "global terrorist" by the US Government. This action affects users of services like noblogs.org.

items.title: 'It's essentially been one long day': A daughter details search for parents in Nepal
items.summary: Shreya Ahuja is appealing for international assistance and improved communications access in Nepal as she searches for her parents, who went missing after devastating floods.

items.title: 4 ways to cope with constant thoughts about your body image
items.summary: Psychologist Diana Hill provides four mental exercises to help individuals manage persistent thoughts about their body image and avoid fixating on their appearance.

items.title: After 6 months of war, Iran's battered regime remains entrenched
items.summary: Six months into a conflict, Iran's regime remains entrenched despite being battered, having adopted an even harder line.

items.title: Experts warn more flooding might hit Nepal. And, Fed chairman to give key address
items.summary: Experts are warning of potential further flooding in Nepal as the death toll from recent flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border rises, while Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is scheduled to deliver a significant address.

items.title: Fed's Kevin Warsh warns inflation is too high, sparking bets rate hikes are coming
items.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh warned about high inflation, leading to expectations of impending rate hikes, although he did not explicitly outline a future path.

items.title: New Jersey is a fossil hotspot, with answers about the day the dinosaurs died
items.summary: A New Jersey suburb has become a significant fossil hotspot, yielding critical data about the asteroid that caused the dinosaurs' extinction, and is now preserved as a fossil park and museum.

items.title: So long to shorts? In Silicon Valley, tech workers are showing less leg
items.summary: A fashion shift in Silicon Valley shows tech workers increasingly opting out of wearing shorts, a trend contrasting with their counterparts in finance who are more frequently showing their legs.

items.title: a16z creates a $1.1B ‘Machine Age’ fund to ‘accelerate the physical buildout of AI’
items.summary: Venture capital firm a16z has established a $1.1 billion "Machine Age" fund dedicated to accelerating the physical buildout of AI hardware, marking a strategic pivot from its traditional software investment focus.

items.title: An Anthropic researcher just gave us a peek at self-improving AI
items.summary: Research by an Anthropic scientist demonstrates that automated systems can enhance performance on ten specific benchmarks for misaligned AI behaviors without negatively impacting overall performance. This suggests progress in creating self-improving AI.

items.title: Anthropic gets its first court win over the Pentagon’s supply-chain risk label
items.summary: Anthropic secured a court victory against the Pentagon, as a federal judge ruled the Trump administration illegally labeled the AI company a supply-chain risk. This is the first win in an ongoing legal dispute.

items.title: Apple TV is raising its subscription prices again
items.summary: Apple TV subscriptions are undergoing another price increase, raising the monthly cost from $12.99 to $14.99.

items.title: Brave’s browser one-ups Chrome with its new support for email aliases
items.summary: Brave browser has introduced support for email aliases, enabling users to register for online services without disclosing their personal email addresses. This feature enhances user privacy.

items.title: Friend-focused photo-sharing app Retro snags $21M
items.summary: Retro, a friend-focused photo-sharing application developed by former Instagram employees, has successfully secured more than $21 million in Series A funding.

items.title: How Sweden built one of Europe’s hottest startup ecosystems
items.summary: Sweden has emerged as a prominent startup ecosystem in Europe, with Cherry Ventures general partner Sophia Bendz providing insights into its development.

items.title: Meta executive leaves for OpenAI as the social media giant faces growing scrutiny in India
items.summary: Sandhya Devanathan, a Meta executive, has departed to join OpenAI, where she will oversee operations in Southeast Asia and Australia, amid Meta's growing scrutiny in India.

items.title: More Americans oppose police license plate cameras than support them: survey
items.summary: A new survey reveals that American opposition to police license plate cameras outweighs support, following numerous reports of law enforcement abusing surveillance tools.

items.title: Neocloud Lambda secures $1B in debt to buy more chips
items.summary: Neocloud Lambda secured $1 billion in private debt to purchase Nvidia AI chips, which it plans to lease to Microsoft, underscoring the significant financial investment required in the current AI boom.

items.title: Open-weight AI companies are the Valley’s hottest acquisition targets
items.summary: Open-weight AI companies are highly sought-after acquisition targets in Silicon Valley, reflecting a substantial influx of capital into the business of distributing AI models freely.

items.title: Ancient Wisdom: I Was the King of the Celebrity Cover Story
items.summary: The author reflects on his career as a celebrity journalist, particularly recalling interviews with Walter Cronkite, whom he respected, and realizing he never wanted to be any of the famous people he profiled, except for Cronkite.

items.title: Can Anyone Beat Abdul El-Sayed?
items.summary: Abdul El-Sayed, Michigan's Democratic Senate nominee, maintains a progressive populist platform and secured a narrow primary victory despite significant opposition from his party's establishment and substantial outside spending. His sharp-tongued responses in interviews continue to challenge opponents.

items.title: Lifestyles of the Rich and Famous: A Summer Special
items.summary: This article observes that despite the dawn of the AI age, people remain fascinated by the opulent lifestyles and decisions of the wealthy, consuming content from influencers and industries catering to them.

items.title: Our Foreign Policy Divide Began with the Korean War
items.summary: Historian Dane J. Cash argues that the Korean War was foundational in shaping America's foreign policy divisions, specifically over isolationism and the exercise of American power, influences that persist in current global conflict discourse.

items.title: TGIF: Have Y’all Never Heard of Noblesse Oblige?
items.summary: This post touches on diverse topics including Dolly Parton, Donald Trump's controversial action of renaming Lake Ontario to "Lake America," and new CBC guidelines discouraging the use of "terrorist attacks" for 9/11. It also highlights a contentious Alaska Senate race featuring two candidates named Dan Sullivan, one accused of attempting voter confusion.

items.title: How to Be a Tree: Notes on the Resilience of Letting Go
items.summary: This essay and poem explore the resilience of trees as a metaphor for life, detailing how they capture light for growth and gracefully let go of leaves in autumn, revealing new buds. It highlights their biological marvels, like photosynthesis and infrared "vision" through phytochromes.

items.title: How to Be Reborn Each Day
items.summary: Drawing on ancient Greek cosmogony and Milton, this piece, featuring Hannah Emerson's poem "Center of the Universe," explores how embracing mental "hellfire" like grief and rage can lead to personal annealing and rebirth. It encourages kissing difficult ideas and finding light in adversity.

items.title: The Four Desires Driving All Human Behavior: Bertrand Russell’s Magnificent Nobel Prize Acceptance Speech
items.summary: Bertrand Russell's Nobel Prize acceptance speech identifies four infinite desires driving human behavior: acquisitiveness, rivalry, vanity, and love of power. He argues these motives, especially the insatiable love of power, profoundly influence human actions and society.

items.title: Apple TV now costs $14.99 a month after its fourth price hike in four years
items.summary: Apple has increased the monthly price of Apple TV+ from $12.99 to $14.99 and the annual subscription to $119, with Apple One also seeing a price hike. This marks the fourth price increase for the streaming service in four years.

items.title: Apple TV’s sci-fi thriller Dark Matter gets even trippier in season 2
items.summary: Season 2 of Apple TV's "Dark Matter" intensifies the sci-fi thriller's drama and thrills, but its complex multiversal premise continues to challenge viewer comprehension. The show focuses on a man who kidnaps an alternate version of himself.

items.title: DLSS 5 leaked and modders are putting Nvidia’s AI effects on everything
items.summary: An unofficial version of Nvidia's DLSS 5 code has leaked from an early-access build of NBA 2K27, leading modders to apply the AI upscaling technology to games like Skyrim, Cyberpunk 2077, and GTA V.

items.title: Google further buries search results under AI mode
items.summary: Google is now automatically expanding its AI search summaries at the top of results pages for some queries, consequently pushing traditional search links much farther down. This change includes a full AI Overview and an "Ask anything" box.

items.title: The GTA VI ‘extended look’ is now streaming on YouTube
items.summary: Rockstar has released an "extended look" at Grand Theft Auto VI on YouTube and its website, following its initial premiere on Netflix. The nearly 27-minute preview highlights the game's atmosphere, protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, and various locations.

items.title: The iPhone Fold could make concerts even worse
items.summary: The Vergecast discussed the implications of a potential iPhone Fold on concert etiquette, along with Apple's new Mac Mini and Mac Studio featuring M6 and M5 Ultra chips. Skepticism was raised regarding Apple's marketing of AI inference capabilities.

items.title: Trump’s EPA wants to let data centers hide their air pollution
items.summary: The EPA under Trump plans to eliminate a federal rule that mandates public notice and comment for industrial air permits, potentially enabling data centers and other industries to proceed with construction without community input on pollution concerns.

items.title: Xbox CEO calls Project Helix a ‘family of devices’
items.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced that Project Helix, previously understood as a single next-generation console, will actually encompass a "family of devices." Further details are expected to be shared soon.
